cover: What to own when a contractor builds your software

slides.title: The copyright
slides.body: Paying for code doesn't make it yours by default. Get a signed IP assignment that covers subcontractors.

slides.title: The repository and its history
slides.body: Code lives in your company's organization from the first commit, with the contractor added as a member.

slides.title: Cloud and hosting accounts
slides.body: Opened by you, billed to your card. The contractor gets a user you can remove without breaking anything.

slides.title: The domain name
slides.body: Registered in your company's name, at a registrar where you hold the login. Your email depends on it too.

slides.title: Every credential
slides.body: Payment, email and app store accounts in your name, with keys in a password manager you control.

slides.title: Documentation you can hand on
slides.body: Could a new engineer run, deploy and change it without calling the contractor? If not, it isn't done.
